subject: PSHE
title: Respectful ways to sort a disagreement
credit: Lesson resource · CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: free for classroom use, share and adapt with credit, no resale
definition: A disagreement means people have different views or wants. In a safe, everyday disagreement, they can listen and look for a fair next step. Respect does not mean having to agree or give in.
routine: Stop the talk for a moment. Use a familiar calm choice or ask for an agreed pause. If anyone feels unsafe, stop and get a trusted adult.
Use I feel ... when ... . I would like ... . Keep to the task and a clear request. No blame, insults or raised voices.
Let the other person respond in their usual way. Check what they mean. Each person can want something different.
4 Agree a next step or ask for help
Choose a fair, safe plan that both can accept. If they cannot agree, ask a trusted adult. They may use an agreed pause and check with staff before a safe return.
i_statement: I feel ... when ... . I would like ... . A clear request can be I would like a turn next. An I statement is not a way to hide blame, such as I feel that you are always wrong.
pause: A learner may say I need a pause. Can we return with staff help? Staff agree the supervised place, support and check-back. Return only when staff and both learners judge the talk safe. Staff can help in another way if a return does not fit. Never walk away alone or return to harm.
safety: Use the routine only for mild, safe disagreements. It is not for threats, harm, repeated unkind treatment or pressure. Stop and tell a trusted adult or school staff if unsafe or unsure. Staff use the safeguarding lead when needed. No one has to solve harm alone or agree to keep peace.
help: Ask a trusted adult or school staff in private. Say Can we talk in private? I need help with a disagreement. Use words, a note, HELP or a usual aid. If the first adult is busy or help is not enough, ask another trusted adult. For an urgent safety concern, get adult help at once through the school route.
step_out: Before teaching, agree a discreet HELP or PAUSE signal, available adult and familiar supervised route. Staff acknowledge it quietly and keep adult support. No public reason is needed. Offer a neutral task, supported return or private catch-up. No learner leaves alone.
safeguarding: Any disclosure goes to the safeguarding lead through school procedure. Listen calmly, reassure, do not probe, investigate or promise secrecy. Follow urgent school procedures for immediate concerns. Keep real concerns and identifying details in the separate safeguarding record, not learning evidence. A pupil unable to identify a trusted adult is supported privately, not pressed.
privacy: All class work and rehearsal use the invented scenes. No real argument, family detail or name is requested. No public account or public speaking is required. A pupil may pass, use an aid or rehearse with staff. Any optional personal card stays with the pupil and is not collected, photographed, displayed or compared.
rehearsal: Offer both invented scenes to every learner. Use pairs with agreed roles, calm voices and no touch. A trusted adult can be the partner; pointing, typing, selecting lines, an aid or exact scribe/readback are equal routes. No forced speech, eye contact, apology, agreement or performance. Stop if uncomfortable. Passing is not failure; record what was actually seen.

cases.title: A model of the routine
cases.text: Two invented learners want the same card shape for a model. Each thinks they should use it first. Both are safe and willing to listen.
cases.model: One learner says I would like a turn next. The other explains they need one short turn. They listen and agree to swap after that turn. They can ask staff for a fair plan if they do not agree.

cases.title: The shared pencil
cases.text: Two invented learners want to use the same colour pencil for a poster. Both need a short turn. Each wants to go first.
cases.statement: I feel cross when I do not know whose turn is next. I would like us to agree a turn.
cases.next: They could agree short turns and a swap cue, or ask staff to help plan turns.

cases.title: The order of two tasks
cases.text: Two invented learners plan a small display. One wants to place the cards first. The other wants to choose the heading first. Both tasks need doing.
cases.statement: I feel stuck when we have two plans. I would like us to choose the first step together.
cases.next: They could hear each reason and agree an order, or take an agreed supervised pause and return with staff help.

same_evidence: Choose a response format, not a scene. Both formats cover both disagreements, an I statement, listening, a fair next step and the pause/help route. Both scenes have a rehearsal opportunity in the lesson. Writing alone is not recorded as spoken or paired rehearsal.

routes.Supported: Keep the routine and model. Use two line choices, word bank and starter for both scenes. Point, type, use a usual aid, staff partner or exact scribe and readback. Record usual access apart from content cues.
routes.Independent: Use the routine and normal aids. Choose calm I statements for both scenes, listen/check, explain a fair plan and the pause/help route. Rehearse with the chosen safe partner or access mode.
routes.Aspire: Compare two fair options in each scene. Adapt the plan if they still cannot agree. Explain when the routine should stop for adult help. Extra reasoning never needs a real personal story.

success: Use four steps for a mild invented disagreement.
Give a clear I statement, listen and suggest a fair next step in both scenes.
Show the agreed pause and adult-help route without having to agree or return to harm.

scaffolds.start: I feel… when… I would like…
scaffolds.model: I feel stuck when we have two plans. I would like a first step.
Add a way to check the other person's view.
Stop and ask a trusted adult for help.

hinge.question: Two learners cannot agree on the first safe task. What fits the routine?
choices: A One must give in so there is no conflict.
B Listen, try a fair plan or ask trusted staff for help.
C Raise their voices until one agrees.
D Walk away alone and never check back.
hinge.parallel: The talk no longer feels safe. A Stop and get trusted adult help. B Keep using the routine until the other person agrees.
hinge.rule: Check privately. B or safe equivalent with a reason: proceed. A makes agreement compulsory; C escalates; D drops safe support and check-back. Re-model and use parallel A. A pass or no response is not observed, never a failure label.

timing: Settle, agree private help/pause; recall different views.
Explain mild disagreement and the four steps, including safety stop.
Model A and I statements; match a step or improve advice.
Check fair choices/safety; choose response format and access.
Scene B22–28; scene C28–34. Offer calm pair/staff/aid rehearsal for both.
Use shared checks, one next step and actual own response.
Explain safe pause/return or help route and close calmly.
where_this_leads: This helps me hear different views, make a fair plan and ask for support in a group or future work.
marking: Retain actual fictional work and the first response. Record usual access separately from adult content prompts, partner/mode and actual rehearsal opportunities. Give one NS and allow the learner's actual response in their own colour or usual mode. E only for actual saved evidence. R only after Voice, Audience, one NS and the actual pupil response. Offer to the Communication portfolio; staff confirm any mapping. Do not infer safe real-world conflict behaviour from a classroom task.
